message:
nothing specific in my notes on tipping, but here's what's actually the case on the ground:

tipping isn't mandatory in [bali](kebi://area/id/bali), but it's genuinely appreciated. most restaurants already add a 10% service charge to the bill, so check before you add more. if there's no service charge, rounding up or leaving 10-15% is normal and welcome.

for drivers, a 10,000-20,000 IDR tip after a longer trip is plenty. for spa and massage, tipping is pretty common since the staff are often on low base wages, 20,000-50,000 IDR is a good range depending on how long the session was. for your villa or hotel staff, leaving something at the end of your stay is a nice touch.

street food and warungs, no expectation at all. the fancier the place, the more a tip lands well.
